title: Ice date interval variance showed no clear change at 77 lake codes between 1951-1980 and 1981-2010
abstract: We tested changes in the variance of the interval from freeze to break-up at 77 lake codes in NSIDC G01377 Version 1. Each code had at least 20 valid frozen seasons in each period, 1951-1980 and 1981-2010. We removed a linear trend from each date within each period. Equal-lake mean interval variance rose from 233.62 to 298.72 days squared. The change was +65.10 days squared, with a conditional 95% shared five-year block interval of -25.03 to +139.09. Thus the test showed no clear change. The exact variance identity gave point changes of +47.43 for freeze variance, +12.43 for break-up variance and +5.24 for minus twice their covariance. Each component interval included zero. One-year and three-year block checks also gave intervals across zero. The mean date interval was 8.66 days shorter in the later period. This is not a measure of continuous ice cover. Selected frozen seasons, missing records, a sample dominated by Finland and short periods limit inference. No physical cause is established. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes, numerical audits and a figure are included. External source records stay outside the package.

display.caption: Changes in equal-lake residual variance from 1951-1980 to 1981-2010 at 77 lake codes. Lines show conditional 95% shared five-year block intervals. All intervals include zero.
